headline: Spatial omics links cell identity, isoform variation and tissue architecture
label: Spatial Multiomics Cell Profiling
summary: Spatial multi-omic methods now register modalities in 3D and resolve isoforms at 500-nm scale, extending single-cell profiling into tissue context.
synthesis: The common thread is the extension of single-cell profiling into spatially resolved, multimodal measurements, supported by computational tools for alignment, visualization and structure-level analysis. MAPS aligns physical and molecular coordinates across modalities, with 3D integration benchmarked on 34 datasets and a 21-million-cell dataset, while VizIt enables multi-view online exploration of single-cell, spatial, epigenomic and genetic data. The sosta Bioconductor package analyses multicellular anatomical structures from spatial omics data. Spatial proteomics and epigenomics yield a tri-omic taxonomy of human hippocampus. What is new is spatial long-read isoform sequencing at 500-nm resolution, which reveals cell-type-specific isoform variability in mouse brain. Other items, including adrenal atlases, prostate basal cell subtypes and vascular functional organisation, apply single-cell or spatial approaches to specific tissues rather than sharing the methodological focus.
